👉 FREE Health and Term Insurance Guidance, without any spam - https://ditto.sh/0imxu0

Did you know that India’s regulator IRDAI designed a standardized health insurance plan that every insurer is mandated to sell? It’s called the Arogya Sanjeevani Health Insurance Plan, and it was launched to simplify health insurance in India and give people an affordable, no-frills option. Unlike other policies filled with complex terms and hidden fine print, the Arogya Sanjeevani is uniform across insurers like HDFC ERGO, Star Health, Care Health, ICICI Lombard, Niva Bupa, and more. The only differences are premiums, claim settlement processes, and customer service quality.

In this video, we’ll do a complete breakdown of the Arogya Sanjeevani Policy 2025. We’ll cover: what makes it unique, what benefits it includes, who should buy it, and most importantly — where it falls short. Think of this as your complete guide to the IRDAI-mandated health insurance plan that’s meant to cut through the noise.

So what does the Arogya Sanjeevani cover? You get basic hospitalization expenses, pre- and post-hospitalization (30 and 60 days), day care procedures, ICU charges, AYUSH treatments, cataract surgery with limits, and even modern treatments like robotic surgery (up to 50% of your sum insured). You also get a cumulative bonus of 5% for every claim-free year, up to 50%. The plan can be taken individually or as a family floater, with sum insureds ranging from ₹50,000 to ₹10 lakh, and it allows lifetime renewals.

But here’s where it stumbles — room rent limits (2% of SI for normal rooms, 5% for ICU), mandatory 5% co-pay on all claims, no restoration benefit, no domiciliary cover, and no add-ons to reduce waiting periods. Plus, waiting periods are standard: 30 days initial, 2 years for listed conditions, and 3 years for pre-existing diseases. In short, it’s affordable and simple, but not flexible enough to deal with today’s rising medical costs.

If you’re buying health insurance for the first time, Arogya Sanjeevani is a good entry-level policy. It’s also useful for people who want a low-cost safety net or those who got rejected from retail policies. But if you’re young, healthy, and eligible for mainstream retail health insurance, plans like HDFC Ergo Optima Secure, Niva Bupa ReAssure 2.0, Aditya Birla Activ One Max, or Care Supreme offer much more value — higher sum insureds, no room rent caps, no co-pays, restoration benefits, and riders that let you customise coverage.

That’s why at Ditto, we rarely recommend Arogya Sanjeevani as a first choice. It’s better than being uninsured, but it’s not the ideal long-term plan. If affordability is your concern, pairing a small retail plan with a super top-up often works out better than relying solely on Sanjeevani.
